items.title: Dave Bennett interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, April 16, 2025
items.q: But you know like we were talking about Benny you know he began classical lessons with Reginald Kell in 1950

ctx.x: And we get so used to taking liberties with our music. We’re making it up a lot of times so it really takes a different kind of concentration I think, to stick to the page.

Big time. I mean you talk about analytical and being right there, I mean that’s a whole different skill set. You know? It’s very challenging. But you know like we were talking about Benny you know he began classical lessons with Reginald Kell in 1950 and he

changed his embouchure, he changed a double lip embouchure and re-invented the way he did it. If you listen to his recordings between 1950 and 1958, he was using the double lip embouchure and if you compare that with the ‘40s, his style changed. It was much more pure, more, you know. And I always thought that he really didn’t need anybody’s help. You know? Because he was such a gifted player. He had that intangible thing that either you have it or you don’t. You know? And he worked so hard to do that, probably in…
